place.zh: 外门演武场 · 五行台
place.en: The outer court training ground · the Five Elements Platform

setup.zh: 宗门大比，内门外门一起比。规矩只三条：掉下台的输，认输的输，执事看着不能再打了的输；半炷香分不出，执事看谁占上风。不许伤人性命。打进前四的进内门名册；头名，得全观一年就这一颗的筑基丹——外门三十年没人拿过。
setup.en: The sect contest, inner court and outer court together. Three rules only: off the stage loses, yielding loses, and if the steward judges you can't go on, you lose; if half a stick of incense settles nothing, the steward judges who has the upper hand. No taking a life. The last four go into the inner register; first place gets the one Foundation pill the whole temple has this year — and the outer court hasn't taken it in thirty years.

recap.zh: 腊月初八，宗门大比开场：内门外门一起比，观主坐在台北面的竹椅上。抽签，你对外门的何七，孙二狗对内门的卢方。你的头一场，何七自己下了台。
recap.en: The eighth of the twelfth month, the sect contest opens, inner court and outer court together, the abbot in a bamboo chair north of the stage. The lots: you against He Qi of the outer court, Sun Ergou against Lu Fang of the inner court. In your first bout He Qi went off the stage by himself.

zh: 腊月初八，宗门大比。观主到了。
规矩三条。前四，进内门名册；头名，筑基丹一枚。
抽签：沈小满，对外门何七。孙二狗，对内门卢方。
en: The eighth of the twelfth month: the sect contest. The abbot has come.
Three rules. The last four go into the inner register; first place, one Foundation pill.
The lots: Shen Xiaoman against He Qi of the outer court. Sun Ergou against Lu Fang of the inner court.

story.zh:
大比的台子搭在外门的演武场上，五块青石板拼成一个圆，缝里都长出了草，名字倒大，叫五行台——台上并没有五行，只有五块石头。演武场四角，立着四棵老柏。宗门大比，内门外门一起比，向来一日打完：内门二十来个练气弟子，外门一百三十来个，两本名册并在一处抽签。外门的人一看内门那二十来个名字，大半都画了圈，末了剩下三十二个，捉对厮杀，输一场便下去。台上的规矩只三条：掉下台的，输；认输的，输；执事看着不能再打了的，输。一场只给半炷香，香到了还分不出，执事看谁占着上风。名录头一页上还有一条，字写得最大：台上不许伤人性命，打死了人，赢了也算输。打进前四的，进内门名册；头名，得那一颗筑基丹。

辰时，观主到了。他从正殿那边一步一步走下来，演武场上两百来号人，说话的、跺脚取暖的，一下子都没了声，连台角那炷香的烟，都直直地立着不晃。他在台北面一张竹椅上坐下，拢着手，面目温和，像来看一场社戏。

抽签的时候，周衡坐在竹筒旁边，捧着大比的名录。那名录是一本老账簿，蓝布面，边角都给翻烂了，前头几十页记的是历年的大比，一年一页，一页上头一行，写的是那一年的冠军——近三十年的，一行一行，都是内门的名字。小满排到周衡跟前，瞧见那名录正翻在前头，墨色从新到旧，旧到后来，黄得像秋天的树叶。有一页上，头名那一行的名字给人拿笔划了一道，划得很直，划过去的墨比字的墨还新些，底下的名字给水渍洇开了，看不清写的是什么。

小满问道：「周师兄，这一个怎么划了？」周衡头也不抬：「划了的，是不在观里了的。」小满道：「死了？」周衡道：「不在观里了。账上只记在不在，不记为什么。为什么，不归我管。」说罢冲他一伸手，「签。」小满把手伸进竹筒里。执事念道：「沈小满——对，外门何七。」轮到孙二狗，执事念道：「孙二狗——对，内门卢方。」台下有人笑出了声。
story.en:
The contest stage stood on the outer court's training ground, five bluestone slabs laid in a circle, grass grown in the seams, and a big name for it: the Five Elements Platform — with no five elements on it, only five stones. At the four corners of the ground stood four old cypresses. The sect contest, inner court and outer court together, was always fought in one day: twenty-odd Qi Refining disciples from the inner court, a hundred and thirty-odd from the outer, two registers drawn as one. Most of the outer court took one look at those twenty-odd inner names and circled their own, leaving thirty-two to be paired off, one loss and out. The stage had only three rules: off the stage, you lose; yield, you lose; if the steward judges you can't go on, you lose. Each bout got half a stick of incense; if it burned out with no result, the steward judged who had the upper hand. On the register's first page was one more rule, in the biggest characters: no taking a life on the stage — kill a man and your win counts as a loss. The last four went into the inner court's register; first place got that one Foundation pill.

At the hour of the dragon the abbot arrived. He came down step by step from the main hall, and the two hundred-odd on the training ground — talking, stamping for warmth — all fell silent at once; even the smoke of the incense at the stage's corner stood straight up without a waver. He sat down in a bamboo chair on the north side of the stage, hands folded in his sleeves, his face mild, like a man come to watch a village opera.

While lots were drawn, Zhou Heng sat by the bamboo tube holding the contest register. It was an old ledger with blue cloth covers, its corners worn to rags; the first few dozen pages recorded past contests, a page a year, and the top line of each the year's champion — for the last thirty years, line after line, inner-court names. At Zhou Heng's table Xiaoman saw the register lying open near the front, the ink going from new to old, old till it was yellow as autumn leaves. On one page the first-place name had been struck through with one straight stroke, the ink of the stroke newer than the name's; the name beneath had blurred in a water stain, past reading.

"Brother Zhou, why is this one struck out?" Zhou Heng didn't look up: "The struck-out ones are the ones no longer at the temple." "Dead?" "No longer at the temple. The books record whether you're here, not why. Why isn't mine to see to." He held out a hand. "Your slip." Xiaoman put his hand in the tube. The steward read out: "Shen Xiaoman — against He Qi of the outer court." Then Sun Ergou's turn: "Sun Ergou — against Lu Fang of the inner court." Someone below laughed out loud.

label.en: Step up: the first bout, against He Qi

exits.means: steps up for the first round; He Qi goes off the stage by himself

story.zh: 小满的头一场，打得最快。何七是进门三年的老弟子，三层，一拳当胸打过来；小满看的是他的脚，脚往前一蹭，他便往旁边一让，顺手在那人背上一推。何七收不住，自己下了台。台下没几个人看清，执事也愣了一下，才道：「沈小满，胜。」
story.en: Xiaoman's first bout was the quickest of the day. He Qi was a disciple three years in, layer three, and he threw a punch straight at the chest; Xiaoman watched his feet, and as the foot slid forward he stepped aside and gave the man's back a push on the way past. He Qi couldn't stop himself and went off the stage on his own. Few below saw it clearly; even the steward hesitated before he said: "Shen Xiaoman wins."
